channel.title: Time and Tide - YOKAI episodes (NHK WORLD-JAPAN)
channel.description: Time and Tide - YOKAI episodes (NHK WORLD-JAPAN) (unofficial feed)

item.title: YOKAI: Exploring Hidden Japanese Folklore — KUCHISAKEONNA
item.description: The Kuchisake-Onna is a Yokai described in Gifu in the 1970s who requests affirmation of her beauty, then reveals a disfigured mouth. We interview locals to learn the background of her appearance. (Available until 2027-10-16)

item.title: YOKAI: Exploring Hidden Japanese Folklore — YAOBIKUNI
item.description: Yaobikuni was said to be a woman in the fishing town of Obama who was given eternal youth after consuming mermaid flesh, but this envied gift instead condemned her to an apparent life of sorrow. (Available until 2027-10-09)

item.title: YOKAI: Exploring Hidden Japanese Folklore - KIJIMUNA
item.description: KIJIMUNA of Okinawa, a red-haired child spirit in banyan trees, brings fortune to fishermen but punishes betrayal, embodying nature in local life. (Available until 2027-10-02)

item.title: YOKAI: Exploring Hidden Japanese Folklore – MUJINA
item.description: In this episode, we pursue the shape-shifting trickster Mujina. This being associated with raccoon dogs is known on Niigata Prefecture's Sado Island as both human and animal, yokai and deity. (Available until 2027-07-10)

item.title: YOKAI: Exploring Hidden Japanese Folklore – UBUME
item.description: The Yokai Ubume was said to be a ghostly woman appearing at night, asking passersby to hold her child under threat of death. We examine how this terrifying figure came to be seen as a sympathetic one. (Available until 2027-07-03)

item.title: YOKAI: Exploring Hidden Japanese Folklore – NAMIKOZO
item.description: This episode features the aquatic Namikozo, which warns locals in the area of the Enshu-nada Sea of coming changes in the weather by beating its drum to give waves a distinct, rumbling tone. (Available until 2027-06-19)

item.title: YOKAI: Exploring Hidden Japanese Folklore - YAROKAMIZU
item.description: In this episode, we search for the Yarokamizu, told of in the Kiso River region of Aichi as a yokai that raises awareness of environmental disasters, and also recognized as a local deity. (Available until 2027-04-17)

item.title: YOKAI: Exploring Hidden Japanese Folklore – KITSUNE
item.description: The fox, or KITSUNE also holds an identity as a supernatural creature commonly depicted at shrines, known for its ability to masquerade as humans to deceive them, or to provide divine messages. (Available until 2026-11-07)
